newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAX to end 1996 bearishly - chartists.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAX to end 1996 bearishly - chartists.

text.p: Technical analysts say they are bearish on the full-year outlook for Germany's 30-share blue-chip DAX index, having revised their 1996 forecast down from a mildly bullish 3,000 points to around 2,380 points.
Bulls are conspicuous by their absence in the range of forecasts by German chartists.
Even the more optimistic technical analysts are expecting the DAX to continue to move sideways for the rest of the year, anticipating little real change between now and early 1997.

The DAX index closed at 2,548.73 points on Monday, up 31.73 points or 1.26 percent, but the trend in recent weeks has been for consolidation. The last time the DAX broke any records was on July 5 when it hit a life high of 2,583.72 points.

"We could see a break in the upwards trend which will shake the bulls out of the market. For the end of 1996 we are forecasting levels of 2,380 points," said Klaus Tafferner, chartist at DG Bank in Frankfurt.
"Short-term indicators like Relative Strength Indicators (RSI) and the Short Range Oscillator are now signalling a downward direction," said Tafferner.
"Looking at the Fibonacci numbers, the 2,546-point level was important as it signalled a turn-around and now we are looking downwards," said Tafferner.

The bearish picture is a change from the pre-summer situation, when some chartists and market commentators more focused on fundamentals were forecasting a rise to over 3,000 points for the end of the year.
The 3,000-point forecast was prevalent when the DAX was hitting record highs on what seemed like every second day.

Giro Olbertz, chartist with Vereins-und-West Bank, said: "I don't think we will hit 3,000 this year, that would need a dramatic upswing. The upwards movements for the rest of the year are going to be moderate ones, it won't be a surging rally."
Tafferner said: "This seems to indicate a continuation of the consolidation period. We see the next medium-term support at 2,450 points."

"Longer term, it seems the correction which began in July is not over yet and even leads one to suspect that long-term support will come at 2,430 points. We will see a further buy signal once we go over the 2,565-point level," said Tafferner.

Klaus Sers, chartist at Vereins-und-West Bank, said: "We are expecting a drop back to 2,300 or 2,350 points over the next couple of weeks and we reckon that the end of year figure will be in or around the 2,500 marks."
One of the main problems facing the DAX over recent months has been a lack of investor interest. Put simply, most investors were on holiday.
There are signs of the basic health of the German share index in the way in which rises in the index are accompanied by higher volumes, with falls accompanied by lower volumes.
With signs of health in evidence, other chartists are still positive on the outlook for the index.
"Volumes should increase from next week when the European holiday season finally comes to a close. Upwards trends of late have been accompanied by higher volumes," said Olbertz.

"In the medium-term the outlook is still positive. The market will not fall under 2,490 points in the mid-term and I reckon that the outlook for the next three months is that we will see the DAX hit 2,650 points," said Olbertz.
